idiom_name: typed puller interface: pull(max, timeoutMs, signal) + AsyncIterable<Message<T>>
implementation_notes: TypeScript contributes the contract rather than new runtime mechanics: the consumer is typed as a puller - pull(max: number, timeoutMs: number, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<Message<T>[]> - so the batch bound and idle timeout are part of the interface instead of conventions, and an AsyncIterable<Message<T>> wrapper lets callers use for-await when they need no control over the pull itself. The runtime is JavaScript's self-rescheduling loop, and acknowledgement stays the application's responsibility, which is where the types pay off: an ack handle that only exists after the handler resolves makes 'acknowledge after processing' checkable by the compiler rather than by review.
pitfalls: The AbortSignal must be threaded through pull, sleep and handler; a signal checked only at the top of the loop leaves the consumer suspended during shutdown.
Types erase at runtime, so Promise<Message<T>[]> says nothing about acknowledgement; the ack contract has to live in the interface (a handle that becomes ackable only after handling) or it drifts.
